newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures spent another lacklustre session trading in a narrow range with the strength of the U.S. bond market setting the positive early tone.
After being marked higher at the open, leaving a gap between 128.54 and 128.74, the March bond contract remained in a 10-tick range, with resistance at 128.94/96 proving too hard to crack.
While traders lamented the lack of business in the run up to the Christmas holiday, most remained positive about the outlook for bonds after the break.
Until business returned to normal traders were still citing a broad range for the contract between 128 and 129.
It was similarly quiet day in the interest rate futures pit with March PIBOR ending unchanged, close to the contract high. Hopes for rate cuts in January kept PIBOR contracts solid.
French industrial production fell in October for the second month in a row, highlighting more economic weakness, supporting the case for some stimulus to the economy, analysts said.
Industrial production excluding energy dropped 0.8 percent in October compared to September, yielding a one percent year-on-year rise, national statistics institute INSEE reported.

Paul Horne, international economist at Smith Barney said, the weakness in consumer goods production was the most worrying part of the report because it reflected weak consumer spending and hinted that production might well remain soft for the rest of the year.
"The consumer remains a problem," he said. "There's a lot of window shopping going on but that's pretty much it. I would think November and December will remain weak."
The franc remained stable on Friday against the mark at 3.3777 compred with 3.3776 on Thursday.
